question.leadin: Answer the following about the landmark interstate commerce case Gibbons v. Ogden.
question.text: This American entrepreneur, nicknamed "Commodore," worked as a steamboat captain and business manager for Gibbons, and combatted other steamboat monopolies before building a railroad empire.
question.clue: During the California Gold Rush, this person created the Accessory Transit Company to bring passengers from the East Coast to San Francisco via Nicaragua.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about the Spanish-American War.
swap.text: One cause of the war was the supposed bombing of this U.S. ship that led to the slogan: "Remember the [blank]!"
swap.clue: In 1976 Hyman Rickover published a book questioning the long-held belief about the cause of its destruction, claiming that Captain Charles Sigsbee's poor supervision of the coal bunker was the real cause.

question.text: The Teller Amendment, the U.S. helps to put down the Boxer Rebellion, and the Treaty of Paris ends the Spanish-American War.
question.clue: This president's campaign manager, Mark Hanna, helped create his successful "front porch campaign."

swap.text: During his second term, Cleveland sent in troops to put down this 1894 strike based on his constitutional responsibility to have mail delivered. This railroad strike was led by Eugene V. Debs.
swap.clue: Mediation offers by the local Civic Federation and Mayor John P. Hopkins were turned down, and violence soon broke out at Blue Island.

question.leadin: Answer the following about labor movements in the U.S.
question.text: This strike pitted the Amalgated Association of Iron and Steel Workers against the Carnegie Steel Company. Henry Clay Frick enlisted Pinkertons to break it up.
question.clue: The leader of the Amalgamated Associations, Hugh O'Donnell, led this strike.

swap.text: Bryan delivered this speech with Biblical imagery including "you shall not press down upon the brow of labor this crown of thorns" in favor of free coinage of silver in 1896.
swap.clue: This speech urged the masses not to "press down upon the brow of labor this crown of thorns" in a condemnation of the gold standard.

question.leadin: According to a story in the New York Times, this politician was caught seducing the Governor of Rhode Island's wife, after which the governor chased him out of his house with a musket.
question.text: Name this 19th-century senator from New York. He led the Stalwart faction of the Republican Party against James G. Blaine's Half-Breeds.
question.clue: He had resigned over the appointment of William Robertson as Collector of the Port of New York by James Garfield, which was presumably a violation of the Treaty of Fifth Avenue that the faction he led agreed to with the Half-Breeds.

swap.leadin: The United States government has a sinister history of massacring Native Americans.
swap.text: This incident took place on the Pine Ridge Indian Reservation in South Dakota. More than 150 men, women, and children from the Lakota Tribe were killed by James Forsyth's 7th Cavalry in this massacre.
swap.clue: This event was sparked by the deaf Black Coyote's refusal to hand over his rifle.

question.leadin: Name these political organizations of New York.
question.text: William Mooney founded this group, which originally utilized elaborate Indian rituals. Its notable leaders included Fernando Wood and Boss Tweed.
question.clue: Samuel Tilden investigated a Grand Sachem ("say-chem") of this organization's corrupt namesake "ring."

swap.leadin: While Brandon, Vermont native Stephen Douglas was unsuccessful in his Presidential bid, two Vermonters did serve in the office. -.
swap.text: What man who claimed a Vermont birth but was accused of being Canadian succeeded from the Vice-Presidency upon the assassination of James Garfield in 1881?
swap.clue: He restructured much of Buchanan's Morrill Tariff with a tariff act labeled the "Mongrel," and accepted a spot on his ticket after the refusal of Levi Morton.

question.leadin: The 1928 Meriam Report's criticism of this law led to its repeal with the Wheeler-Howard Act in 1934.
question.text: Name this 1887 law that forced Native American tribes with traditional usage of communal land to switch to individual ownership of private property. Through this act, the US government stole 100 million acres of tribal land.
question.answerHtml: Dawes Act [or Dawes Severalty Act of 1887; or General Allotment Act]
question.clue: This 1887 act allowed the U.S. government to survey Indian tribal lands and divide them up among the individuals in the tribe to assimilate Indians into American society.

swap.text: This man repeatedly made the dubious claim that he completed a grueling 322-mile marathon run while working for the Pony Express. Annie Oakley worked as a sharpshooter on a traveling show run by this man.
swap.answerHtml: Buffalo Bill [or Buffalo Bill Cody or William Frederick Cody]
swap.clue: He inspired Theodore Roosevelt with his pro-manhood "Congress of Rough Riders" tour.

question.text: Chicago businessman Montgomery Ward, a competitor of this man, financed early Grange consumer cooperatives in the 1870s. After retiring, this man left his mail-order business to Julius Rosenwald.

swap.text: This sometime-rival of Blaine became a national hero in Paraguay after arbitrating the Chaco in the War of the Triple Alliance. Reconstruction ended after the Compromise of 1877 elected this man president over Samuel Tilden.
swap.clue: Specie payment resumed under this president, whose Secretary of the Treasury was John Sherman.

question.leadin: This event is often credited with ending open-range ranching.
question.text: Identify this nickname given to the brutal winter of 1886 and 1887 which saw more than half a million cattle die on the Northern Plains.

swap.leadin: The Hayden Expedition to this location issued propaganda that its natives were afraid of geysers to increase tourism.
swap.text: Name this first U.S. national park that was established in 1872.
swap.clue: One early success of the conservationist movement was the designation of this first national park, located primarily in Wyoming. The Old Faithful geyser can be found in this park.

question.text: This institution in Upstate New York was founded by Lewis Miller and John Heyl Vincent as a teaching camp for Sunday school teachers. It included Palestine Park, a scale model of the Holy Land.
question.clue: This institution that names a late 19th-century adult education movement whose lecturers and entertainers, including Russell Conwell, reached 35 million people on its "circuit."

swap.leadin: Flood v. Kuhn upheld baseball's exemption from this lype of legislation, though several justices noted that not classifying the sport as interstate commerce in the first place didn't make much sense.
swap.text: Name this type of law, exemplified by the Sherman and Clayton acts.
swap.clue: MLB was granted an exemption from one of these laws, which was first successfully used against the Northern Securities Company.

question.text: Identifying "democratic" and "legislative" types of government, this speech given in Chicago at the DNC of 1896 ends with the speaker claiming "you shall not crucify mankind" on the title object.

swap.text: The phrase "For King and Country" had earlier been used to title an editorial condemning one of these massive work stoppages that occurred in Britain in 1926.
swap.clue: One of these events coinciding with an Intervision Song Contest started after poor treatment of Anna Walentynowicz ("VAL-en-TIN-oh-vitch") at the Lenin Shipyards.
